what_is_supported: FULL TEXT READ 2026-09-22. PROGESTERONE UP-REGULATES MUC1, IT DOES NOT SWITCH IT OFF: a twofold MUC1 mRNA increase in receptive (Day 21) versus non-receptive (Day 13) endometrium, p<0.05, with protein appearing as a continuous apical array after 6 d of progesterone. MUC1 removal is STRICTLY LOCAL: it is absent from epithelium subjacent and adjacent to the attached embryo and rises with distance from the implantation site, with cytokeratin confirming the epithelium is intact. In luminal epithelium the Day-21 up-regulation is detected by BC-3 where BC-2 cannot detect it, i.e. core protein rises while a glycosylation-sensitive epitope is lost.
what_is_NOT_supported: DOES NOT LICENSE A SIGN FLIP, AND DOES NOT LICENSE AN EMBRYO-COMPETENCE CONJUNCT. The mechanism of local removal is undetermined - the authors concede embryo-induced epithelial apoptosis would look the same - and the adhesion-phase observation is n=3 sites, descriptive, with no perturbation. Arrested embryos were compared only in the APPOSITION coculture, where their effect was intermediate; they were not tested at attachment. Glycoform, abundance and local clearance are three different measurements here and the paper does not collapse them. No stromal endpoint.
